comment: What a hosted connector's caller proxy answers when it refuses a caller (ADR-0168 decision 7), and what the runner reads back to name the refusal. The proxy (apps/worker/src/curie_connector_proxy/server.py) answers every refusal with `status` and a JSON-RPC error body, never contacts the connector, and sends no WWW-Authenticate: a 401 sends the bundled Claude CLI into OAuth discovery and client registration against the connector, and a 403 does not. The MCP client surfaces a JSON-RPC error body at a non-2xx status as the request's error, so the runner (runner/src/curie_runner/mcp_tool_capability.py) finds `error.data.curie_caller` and reports the refusal by name. `header` is the request header the token travels in. `unpaired` and `duplicate_header` are driven through the real proxy; their tokens are cct2 (tests/vectors/connector-caller-token.json) signed by that corpus's first seed. Read by apps/worker/tests/test_connector_proxy.py and runner/tests/test_mcp_tool_capability_caller.py, which reject an unknown key so a key added for one reader cannot pass vacuously. Every token (`unpaired.token` and each `duplicate_header.tokens` entry) is stored as its "."-separated segments, exactly token.split("."), so no single high-entropy token string appears in the corpus, and readers join them with ".".

unpaired.why: A validly signed cct2 token that carries run without work_item is malformed and refused as invalid.

duplicate_header.why: Two X-Curie-Caller headers are refused as invalid even when each token alone would be admitted under `admits` at `now`, so the proxy never has to choose one.

error.message: caller refused: no caller token was presented
caller refused: the caller token is not valid
caller refused: the caller token has expired
caller refused: this agent is not admitted by the connector
caller refused: the connector tool call has no matching grant
